report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. Initiating tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) in the third trimester for pregnant women with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and high viral load significantly reduces mother-to-child transmission (MTCT).

### Supporting Evidence
* **Clinical Trials:** A major randomized trial by Pan et al. (2016) demonstrated that starting TDF at 28–32 weeks gestation reduced MTCT to 0% at 28 weeks postpartum compared to 7% in the control group, despite all infants receiving hepatitis B vaccine and immune globulin (HBIG).
* **Global Guidelines:** Meta-analyses confirm these benefits, leading the World Health Organization (WHO) and major liver societies to recommend TDF starting in the third trimester for pregnant women with HBV DNA $\ge 200,000\text{ IU/mL}$.

### Counter-Evidence & Context
* **Individually Non-Significant Trials:** A trial by Jourdain et al. (2018) in Thailand observed transmission in 0/147 infants in the TDF group versus 3/147 in the placebo group, a difference that did not achieve statistical significance ($p = 0.25$). 
* **Explanation:** When timely infant immunoprophylaxis (birth-dose vaccine plus HBIG) is administered with near-100% adherence, baseline transmission rates are already low, making single-trial statistical differences harder to detect. However, aggregated evidence confirms TDF provides critical additional protection against maternal breakthrough infections.

### Sources
* WHO Guidelines: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK561126/
* Pan et al. (2016 Trial): https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1508660
* Jourdain et al. (2018 Trial): https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1708131
* Systematic Review: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11478587/
